sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 1999. Warembori. Annotated draft of Languages of the World/Materials 341 (Munich: Lincom), 76 pp., MPI-EVA copy.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6621.W28 D65 1999)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6621.W28 D65 1999
sources.note: Only about Warembori, not Pauwi: 'Stress is normally assigned to the penultimate syllable of a word or compound' (section 2.2, p. 7-8), with exceptions for nasal-final roots, all-identical vowels (final stress) and 'heavy' consonants. Pauwi appears only in the bibliography (Van der Aa 1885); section 1.1 speaks of 'a no-longer extant language which was related to Yoke' as a source of Warembori vocabulary.

sources.citation: Wikipedia articles 'Yoke language' and 'Lower Mamberamo languages' (read 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No stress information. The Yoke article states that the 19th-century 'Pauwi' wordlist collected by Robidé van der Aa at Lake Rombebai 'is transparently Yoke' and lists Pauwi as an alternative designation of Yoke; its Yoke phonology section has no prosody.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald & Sebastian Nordhoff. 2012. The languages of Melanesia: Quantifying the level of coverage. In Nicholas Evans & Marian Klamer (eds.), Melanesian Languages on the Edge of Asia: Challenges for the 21st Century (Language Documentation & Conservation Special Publication 5), 13-33 + online appendix (per-language status and source list). Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing on Pauwi prosody. A documentation-coverage survey: Pauwi is counted as a separate, presumed-extinct language whose most extensive description is a wordlist; the main text's only tone content is general (Wurm 1954, Donohue 1997, Cahill 2011 surveys, p. 20), not about Pauwi. Useful for identity: the authors split Moszkowski's (1913) Pauwi from Robidé van der Aa's (1885) 'Pauwi' list, which they assign to Yoke [yki]; the appendix source list for Pauwi equals Glottolog's. The 'Stroeve' in the table label was followed up (Feuilletau de Bruyn, Opperman, Doorman & Stroeve 1915, TKNAG 32: 655…

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane, Mark Donohue & Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078. Dallas: SIL.
sources.note: The most recent first-hand survey of the Yoke/Warembori area; may settle whether the 1885 'Pauwi' list is Yoke (Wikipedia cites it for Yoke), which decides whether any future Yoke phonology could stand in for Pauwi. Not expected to contain a stress statement for Pauwi itself.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. Entry 152 'PAUWI ISOLATE', pp. 52-53.
sources.note: Nothing. 'It is doubtful whether the language is still spoken. When first recorded, Pauwi was spoken by an estimated 100 people living in a village on the Mamberamo River at about 25 kilometers from the sea.. The two short wordlists on hand share a few probable cognates with Warenbori, Tarunggare, Baropasi, Kwerba and the Tor languages.. Sources: Robidé van der Aa 1885 (Wl); Moszkowski 1911 (N); Anonymous 1913 (Wl).' No Pauwi wordlist reproduced.

sources.citation: Anonymous [Max Moszkowski]. 1913. Wörterverzeichnisse von Papua-Sprachen aus Holländisch-Neuguinea. Anthropos 8: 254-259 (Analecta et Additamenta).
sources.note: No statement. Four-column wordlist (Borumessu, Koassa, Pauwi, Südfluss) plus a Pauwi supplement on p. 259; the Pauwi forms carry acute accents on one syllable (passára 'Schädel', pamabúna 'Bart', péro 'Schwein', suába 'Kasuar', oschénu 'eins', biméssi 'drei', kinguéri 'wir zwei', bimbájo, tabáko), which is the German ethnographers' convention for the stressed syllable, but the text never says so and gives no rule; the only remark is 'Pauwi (anscheinend mit Nufoor Elementen gemischt)' (p. 254).

sources.citation: Dryer, Matthew S. (compiler). ASJP wordlists PAUWI_2 (from Anonymous/Moszkowski 1913) and PAUWI_3 (from Robidé van der Aa 1885). In Wichmann, Holman & Brown (eds.), The ASJP Database. asjp.clld.org.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: ASJP orthography carries no stress; no notes on prosody; this is the only trace of Dryer's handling of Pauwi that is online (the 'comparative materials' wished for in our bibliography are not deposited anywhere reachable).

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1912. Notes on languages in the east of Netherlands New Guinea. Appendix C in A. F. R. Wollaston, Pygmies and Papuans: the Stone Age to-day in Dutch New Guinea, 322-345. London: Smith, Elder & Co.
sources.note: Nothing on sounds or accent. p. 323: 'there is more information of the language of Pauwi at the mouth of the.. Mamberamo River, where F. van Braam Morris collected a vocabulary published by Robide van der Aa in 1885. This was considered faulty by de Clercq.' p. 325: 'The Sentani and Pawi languages seem to have very few or no words similar to the Indonesian, and may probably be found to be Papuan languages. But nothing is known of the grammar.' Comparative vocabulary (pp. 337 ff.) has a Pauwi column without stress marks.

sources.citation: Moszkowski, Max. 1911-1912. Vorläufiger Bericht über die Deutsche Mamberamo-Expedition in Niederländisch-Neu-Guinea. Zeitschrift der Gesellschaft für Erdkunde zu Berlin 1911(3): 185-192; 1912(4): 271-288; 1912(5): 365-377.
sources.note: No linguistic data; 1911 p. 191 only says 'dass ich mich von vornherein bemüht hatte, die am Ufer des Mamberamo gesprochenen Sprachen aufzunehmen'; 1912 parts mention Pauwi for meteorological notes and distances.

sources.citation: Moszkowski, Max. 1911. Die Völkerstämme am Mamberamo in Holländisch-Neuguinea und auf den vorgelagerten Inseln. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 43: 315-346.
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic lecture; no wordlist. p. 318 only says the coastal languages are Malayo-Polynesian and names Numfor/Windessi; p. 321-322 says the Pauwi people count only to five; p. 332 says the village Pauwi (25 km upstream) was half interior 'Pauwi' people and half coastal Bossumassin, children speaking the mother's language.

sources.citation: Rouffaer, G. P. 1909. De drie opvaarten der Mambèramo (Noord Nieuw-Guinea), Juli 1884, Jan. 1900 en Juni 1906. Tijdschrift van het Koninklijk Nederlandsch Aardrijkskundig Genootschap, 2e serie, 26: 86-128, with Bijlagen (A: Kerkhoven's 1884 journal incl. 'Een woordenlijstje der taal van Pauwi', alphabetised) and kaart IV.
sources.note: No phonology content: Rouffaer's synthesis of the 1884, 1899-1900 and 1906 ascents plus Kerkhoven's journal; the c. 60-item Pauwi wordlist is reprinted alphabetically without accent marks and without any remark on pronunciation ('Dit Woordenlijstje nam Robidé van der Aa vroeger van Kerkhoven reeds over, doch niet alphabetisch.. Volledigheidshalve moge het ook hier volgen'). The 1906 Brak report's remark 'Hunne taal bestaat uit zeer veel harde klanken en diepe keelgeluiden' concerns people met near Morris-eiland upstream, not Pauwi.

sources.citation: Van Hasselt, J. L. 1886. Een tocht naar de rivier Amberno, gelegen op de Noordwestkust van Nieuw-Guinea, 138° O. L. Tijdschrift van het Nederlandsch Aardrijkskundig Genootschap, 2e serie, deel III, Afdeeling Verslagen en Aardrijkskundige Mededeelingen, 180-186 (communicated by P. J. B. C. Robidé van der Aa).
sources.note: No phonology. Only affiliation remarks (p. 185-186): 'Wat betreft de taal, door de bevolking gesproken, deze verschilt geheel, niet slechts van 't Ansoesch, Wandamsch en Waropensch, maar ook van de taal van het niet zoozeer verwijderde Koeroedoe.. [ik had mij] bezig gehouden met 't vertalen van een woordenlijst.. in die drie talen of dialecten.. maar slechts zeer zelden was er overeenstemming'. Also: river name Mamberaminoe 'groot water'; a Pauwi man understood a few words of Kurudu.

sources.citation: Bonaparte, Roland. 1885. Les récents voyages des Néerlandais à la Nouvelle-Guinée. Versailles (offprint; also in Comptes rendus des séances de la Société de géographie 1885).
sources.note: Nothing; a bibliographic notice only. Gallica ContentSearch finds 'Pauwi' on views 17, 26, 27; views 26-27 are voyage narrative ('Les habitants de ce kampong appelé Pauwi s'apprivoisèrent assez facilement..'). The word list itself is not reprinted on the pages seen.

sources.citation: Robidé van der Aa, P. J. B. C. 1885. Reizen van D. F. van Braam Morris naar de Noordkust van Nederlandsch Nieuw-Guinea. Eerste vaart op de Amberno- of Rochussen-rivier. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde van Nederlandsch-Indië 34: 73-114; Bijlage 'Woordenlijstje der taal van Pauwi (benedenloop der Rochussen-Rivier)', pp. 111-114.
sources.note: Nothing. About 60 words plus numerals ('kait pasari' one, 'kait pari' two..) taken from Mr Kerkhove's 1884 journal; the words are printed in italics without accent marks (p. 114 checked as a page scan); Van der Aa's remarks (pp. 111-113) concern only the numerals and possible Mafoor/Numfor affinities.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x record for Pauwi [pauw1243] and reference records 120677, 95108, 17111, 126692, 64567, 148303, 303414; family pages yoke1239, lowe1409, yoke1238.
sources.note: Nothing. All four Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are rated 'a wordlist or less' (Moszkowski 1911, Anon. 1913, Galis 1955, Voorhoeve 1975); status Extinct (AES 10); subclassification comments cite Jones 1987, Donohue 1999, Le Roux n.d., none of whose language code fields list Pauwi.
